properties.statement: Every integer datetime.* output is in its §9.2 range: month 1..12, day 1..(days in that month) ⊆ 1..31, hour 0..23, minute 0..59, second 0..59, day_of_year 1..(days in that year) ⊆ 1..366, is_leap_year 0 or 1.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, (1 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.month.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.month.exact t) ≤ 12) ∧ (1 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.day.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.day.exact t) ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.monthLength (Esm.Closed.Datetime.isLeapYear (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t)) (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.month.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.day.exact t) ≤ 31) ∧ (0 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.hour.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.hour.exact t) ≤ 23) ∧ (0 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.minute.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.minute.exact t) ≤ 59) ∧ (0 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.second.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.second.exact t) ≤ 59) ∧ (1 ≤ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.dayOfYear.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.dayOfYear.exact t) ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.yearLength (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.dayOfYear.exact t) ≤ 366) ∧ ((Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.isLeapYear.exact t) = 0 ∨ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.isLeapYear.exact t) = 1)

properties.statement: The floor-divmod by 86400: t = 86400·⌊t/86400⌋ + tod with 0 ≤ tod < 86400 (Python-style floored modulo).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, t = 86400 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t : ℝ) + Esm.Closed.Datetime.timeOfDay t ∧ 0 ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.timeOfDay t ∧ Esm.Closed.Datetime.timeOfDay t < 86400

properties.statement: The decomposition round-trips to the real instant floor: 86400·days(year, month, day) + 3600·hour + 60·minute + second = ⌊t⌋ (hour/minute/second from ⌊time-of-day⌋, ruling Q-3).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, 86400 * Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨(Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t), (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.month.exact t), (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.day.exact t)⟩ + 3600 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.hour.exact t) + 60 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.minute.exact t) + (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.second.exact t) = ⌊t⌋

properties.statement: civil-from-days and days-from-civil are inverse: every day number maps to a valid date and back, and every valid date maps to a day number and back.
properties.lean_statement: (∀ n : ℤ, Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil (Esm.Closed.Datetime.civilFromDays n) = n ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.civilFromDays n).Valid) ∧ ∀ c : Esm.Closed.Datetime.Date, c.Valid → Esm.Closed.Datetime.civilFromDays (Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil c) = c

properties.statement: The day count is the proleptic-Gregorian calendar: day 0 is 1970-01-01; consecutive days, months of the standard lengths (February 28/29), and years of 365 days, or 366 when divisible by 4 and not by 100 unless by 400, follow one another with no gaps.
properties.lean_statement: Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨1970, 1, 1⟩ = 0 ∧ (∀ y m d : ℤ, Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y, m, d + 1⟩ = Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y, m, d⟩ + 1) ∧ (∀ y m : ℤ, 1 ≤ m → m ≤ 11 → Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y, m + 1, 1⟩ = Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y, m, Esm.Closed.Datetime.monthLength (Esm.Closed.Datetime.isLeapYear y) m⟩ + 1) ∧ (∀ y : ℤ, Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y + 1, 1, 1⟩ = Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨y, 12, 31⟩ + 1) ∧ (∀ (l : Bool) (m : ℤ), Esm.Closed.Datetime.monthLength l m = if m = 2 then (if l then 29 else 28) else if m = 4 ∨ m = 6 ∨ m = 9 ∨ m = 11 then 30 else 31) ∧ (∀ y : ℤ, Esm.Closed.Datetime.yearLength y = if (4 ∣ y ∧ ¬ 100 ∣ y) ∨ 400 ∣ y then 366 else 365)

properties.statement: is_leap_year(t) = 1 exactly when the year of t has 366 days, exactly when it has a February 29, and exactly when the year is divisible by 4 and not by 100, or by 400.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, ((Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.isLeapYear.exact t) = 1 ↔ Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨(Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t) + 1, 1, 1⟩ - Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨(Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t), 1, 1⟩ = 366) ∧ ((Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.isLeapYear.exact t) = 1 ↔ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.Date.Valid ⟨(Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t), 2, 29⟩)) ∧ ((Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.isLeapYear.exact t) = 1 ↔ (4 ∣ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t) ∧ ¬ 100 ∣ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t)) ∨ 400 ∣ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t))

properties.statement: day_of_year agrees with month and day (days before the month plus the day) and counts from January 1 of the same year (1 = Jan 1).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.dayOfYear.exact t) = Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysBeforeMonth (Esm.Closed.Datetime.isLeapYear (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t)) (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.month.exact t) + (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.day.exact t) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.dayOfYear.exact t) = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t - Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨(Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.exact t), 1, 1⟩ + 1

properties.statement: The integer outputs are monotone in t: t ≤ t' implies (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) at t is lexicographically ≤ the same at t'.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t t' : ℝ, t ≤ t' → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fieldsKey t ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.fieldsKey t'

properties.statement: Each integer datetime.* function returns its exact value when it fits in Int32 and raises closed_function_overflow exactly when it does not.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (f : Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn) (t : ℝ), f.eval t = .overflow ↔ ¬ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.int32Min ≤ f.exact t ∧ f.exact t ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.int32Max)

properties.statement: Only datetime.year can overflow (every other result, is_leap_year included, is a small bounded integer), and it overflows exactly for t before -2147483648-01-01T00:00:00Z or at/after 2147483648-01-01T00:00:00Z.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (f : Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn) (t : ℝ), (f ≠ .year → f.eval t = .ok (f.exact t)) ∧ (Esm.Closed.Datetime.IntFn.year.eval t = .overflow ↔ t < 86400 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨Esm.Closed.Datetime.int32Min, 1, 1⟩ : ℝ) ∨ 86400 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil ⟨Esm.Closed.Datetime.int32Max + 1, 1, 1⟩ : ℝ) ≤ t)

properties.statement: On and after -4800-03-01 (Gregorian) the Fliegel–van Flandern JDN, with its published truncating division, is the day count plus 2440588 (the JDN of 1970-01-01).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ c : Esm.Closed.Datetime.Date, c.Valid → Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil Esm.Closed.Datetime.fvfFirstDate ≤ Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil c → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fvfJdn c = Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil c + 2440588

properties.statement: Everywhere (every valid proleptic-Gregorian date), the FvF JDN is within 3 days of the day count plus 2440588.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ c : Esm.Closed.Datetime.Date, c.Valid → |Esm.Closed.Datetime.fvfJdn c - (Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil c + 2440588)| ≤ 3

properties.statement: On and after -4800-03-01T00:00:00Z the spec's reference julian_day (FvF on the date plus (tod − 43200)/86400, exact arithmetic) is the standard continuous Julian Date t/86400 + 2440587.5.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, 86400 * (Esm.Closed.Datetime.daysFromCivil Esm.Closed.Datetime.fvfFirstDate : ℝ) ≤ t → Esm.Closed.Datetime.julianDay t = t / 86400 + 2440587.5

properties.statement: For every t, the spec's reference julian_day equals the standard Julian Date t/86400 + 2440587.5 (§9.2: 'the standard JDN convention (JD 0 = noon UTC on 4713 BC Jan 1, proleptic Julian)').
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.Closed.Datetime.julianDay t = t / 86400 + 2440587.5
properties.note: False in the model: Esm.Closed.Datetime.julianDay_ne_standard proves the negation (on -4800-02-29 the published FvF formula is one day ahead; it is exact only from -4800-03-01, P-closed-datetime-fvf-domain). Not marked refuted because a refutation needs a reproducer: this needs a spec question choosing between 'FvF as published' (the spec's reference computation) and 'the standard JD' (the spec's convention) for dates before -4800-03-01; reported to the coordinator.
properties.question: Q-99

properties.statement: The result of a datetime.* function at a NaN or infinite t_utc.
properties.note: §9.2 says all real-valued time inputs are binary64 but gives no result or diagnostic for NaN/±Inf (§9.4 lists 'NaN input' among example boundary cases). The adapter reports error nonfinite_input; needs a spec question.
properties.question: Q-100

properties.statement: Binary64 claim (a), precise range: for every double t with |t| < 2^60, ⌊fl(t/86400)⌋ = ⌊t/86400⌋, except the negative t with t/86400 underflowing to zero, -43200·2^-1074 ≤ t < 0.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.F64.IsF64 t → |t| < 2 ^ (60 : ℤ) → ¬ (-(43200 * 2 ^ (-1074 : ℤ)) ≤ t ∧ t < 0) → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fDayNumber t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t

properties.statement: In the underflow band -43200·2^-1074 ≤ t < 0 the binary64 floor is one day late: t/86400 rounds to 0 (day 0, 1970-01-01) while ⌊t/86400⌋ = -1.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, -(43200 * 2 ^ (-1074 : ℤ)) ≤ t → t < 0 → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fDayNumber t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t + 1

properties.statement: The 2^60 bound on claim (a) is nearly tight: t = 86400·(2^44 + 1) − 128 (about 1.52e18 s, a double below 2^61) has t/86400 rounding up to the integer 2^44 + 1.
properties.lean_statement: ¬ ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.F64.IsF64 t → |t| < 2 ^ (61 : ℤ) → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fDayNumber t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t

properties.statement: For every double t with |t| ≤ 2^59 outside (−43200, 0), the binary64 floor-divmod (d = ⌊t ⊘ 86400⌋, tod = t ⊖ 86400 ⊗ d) is exact, so every integer output equals the exact model's.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.F64.IsF64 t → |t| ≤ 2 ^ (59 : ℤ) → ¬ (-43200 < t ∧ t < 0) → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fDayNumber t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t ∧ Esm.Closed.Datetime.fTimeOfDay t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.timeOfDay t ∧ Esm.Closed.Datetime.fSecondOfDay t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.secondOfDay t

properties.statement: §9.2's claim that the floor-divmod by 86400 gives zero drift on the integer outputs, for the binary64 floor-divmod: for every double |t| ≤ 2^59 the binary64 day and ⌊tod⌋ equal the exact ones.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.F64.IsF64 t → |t| ≤ 2 ^ (59 : ℤ) → Esm.Closed.Datetime.fDayNumber t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.dayNumber t ∧ Esm.Closed.Datetime.fSecondOfDay t = Esm.Closed.Datetime.secondOfDay t
properties.note: Counterexample t = -1 - 2^-52: 86400 + t rounds to 86399, so the binary64 ⌊tod⌋ is 86399 (23:59:59) where the exact one is 86398 (23:59:58). The fixture scenario that exercises this class is frac_pre_epoch_minute_1969_12_31T23_59_below_ulp (t = -60.00000000000001: binary64 pipeline second 0, exact 59), added on formal/p1-bind-datetime. In the underflow band the binary64 time of day is t itself, negative, so a binding that uses it reports hour -1 (P-closed-datetime-binary64-floor-underflow; scenario frac_epoch_below_ulp, t = -5e-324). Bindings must compute ⌊tod⌋ as ⌊t⌋ - 86400·d in integers (secondOfDay_eq) to meet ruling Q-3.

properties.statement: Binary64 claim (b), stated precisely: the spec's binary64 julian_day (JDN ⊕ ((tod ⊖ 43200) ⊘ 86400), with d = ⌊t ⊘ 86400⌋ and tod = t ⊖ 86400 ⊗ d) is within 1 ulp of the exact real value of the same formula on the exact (day, tod) pair, ulp taken at the exact value, for every double |t| ≤ 2^59 (the underflow band and (−43200, 0) included). Within the 1 ulp: the final add contributes at most half an ulp, the divide and the earlier subtractions together at most another half.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ t : ℝ, Esm.F64.IsF64 t → |t| ≤ 2 ^ (59 : ℤ) → |Esm.Closed.Datetime.fJulianDay t - Esm.Closed.Datetime.julianDay t| ≤ Esm.F64.ulp (Esm.Closed.Datetime.julianDay t)
